defects.claim_says: The conditions imported from the Cotton Textile approval are incorporated as they stood and add no end of their own; no held record shows an earlier end, so the first end is 1935-06-14.
defects.source_says: Held EO 6206 (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6206-code-fair-competition-for-the-cotton-textile-industry.txt, July 16, 1933) records that the Cotton Textile approval of July 9, 1933 carried 'condition 12 of said order providing for the termination of approval at the end of four months unless expressly renewed', withdrawn only on July 16, 1933 and only for the Cotton Textile code. EO 6204-A (July 14, 1933) approved the Rayon Weaving provisions 'subject to the interpretations and conditions imposed by me on my approval of the corresponding provisions of said Cotton Textile Code', so as they stood on July 14 the imported conditions included a four-month termination. The claim neither addresses this possible own-terms end (about November 1933, unless renewed or unless the July 16 withdrawal carried over) nor records it as a gap.

Whether the imported four-month termination condition applied to this partial approval, and whether any renewal or later Rayon Weaving action followed (the July 9 order and any renewal are not held), is a material open question on the first end. The parallel partial approval of the Throwing Industry the same day (EO 6204-B) was followed by a full approval (EO 6331-E, WPA p. 543), which shows interim approvals of this form were superseded; for Rayon Weaving none is held, which is absence of evidence, not proof.
